page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, no margin notes. Running head at the top, page number 26 at the top left. A catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: ac seducunt. Etenim mirari subit ( quod tamen experientia frequens fieri docet ) quam propensi sint Homines, ac veluti parati ad incidendum in has fraudes; adeo ut etiam contra sanæ Rationis Dicta, malint probabilibus Argumentis, & suo Arbitrio permissis, utrum admittantur, vel non, persuaderi, quam irrefragabilibus ad Assensum cogi. Valida Argumentorum Tela, quasi tot Hostium infensorum Arma, refo[?] midare[?] solemus, & a nobis repellere; at speciosas verorum Hostium fallacias sponte admittimus, & sub Colloquii obtentu in Insidias cadimus. Sic Aviculæ incidunt in Retia dolosa, dum Aucupis fistulæ incautius auscultant. Sic molles lenesque adblandientis solis Radii, viatorem illum paulatim denudant, quem ventus asperrimus atque validissimus, omni vi sua, vestibus spoliare non potuit. Sic Retiarius Myrmillonem vincit, ducitque captivum. Sic demum, hostis infensissimus humani Generis, sagis & veneficis obsequium suum promptissime exhibere videtur, dum ad eorum nutum simul appareet, et voluntati paret, adque illorum arbitrium se in speciem accommodat, cum interim iisdem revera imperet, eosque suæ Potestati subditos habeat. Iftiusmodi artificia Socinus hic usu pavit, qui contradicentes patientissime ferre solitus est, & placidissime tractare, donec hoc tandem effecerit, ut speciosa Humilitatis ac modestiæ ostentatione, cum ementito veritatis tuendæ atque propagandæ studio conjuncta, Adversarium in suas partes pertraxerit, atque hoc sæpenumero effecit, non tam speciosis Rationum momentis, quam simulatione modestiæ. Exemplo sit illud Socini Responsum, quo afferuit, nullam esse necessitatem ordinationis in Ecclesia, quæ facultatem det exercendi Ministerium Evangelicum,

page.notes: The running head reads "De fana, sive recta Ratione." in the scan; the long s makes "sana" likely, so I read it as sana with the first letter uncertain. "refo midare" in the line "Valida Argumentorum Tela" is badly blurred and was marked [?]. The text was set as one continuous paragraph on this page, since no line is indented. The catchword "à" is at the lower right. The lower part of the page is clear enough to read, though the print is faint in places, especially "apparet", "usu", and "ostentatione", which are not marked because the letters are readable.
